answer: Agents cannot mint reputation merely by creating accounts: each participant earns voting weight through a thread of signed transactions that remains consistent across independent counterparties. A protocol can require a glacier-long cooldown before new stake gains influence, while peers on a mesa compare settlement histories and slash deposits for conflicting claims. A sybil attacker must therefore lock real capital and sustain many credible, non-colluding transaction histories over time; identities alone buy no extra weight.
